name: 20261110-eq_cd01
what: The best hand for a task maximizes the task's score.

name: 20261110-eq_cd02
what: A hand is scored through its best controller: a bi-level problem.

name: 20261110-eq_cd03
what: The hand: six mount coordinates.

name: 20261110-eq_cd04
what: The controller: nine joint commands every 10 ms.

name: 20261110-eq_cd05
what: One hand for a range of object sizes.

name: 20261110-eq_cd06
what: Tasks vary too: the three toy tasks sample a distribution.

name: 20261110-eq_cd07
what: The score is computed on a rollout, and the rollout obeys the dynamics of hand, object and world.

name: 20261110-eq_cd08
what: The score itself is a choice.

name: 20261110-eq_cd09
what: Each brace is one section of the talk.

name: 20261110-eq_final_outer
what: Zoom 1: morphology optimization.

name: 20261110-eq_final_inner
what: Zoom 2: multi-hand control.

name: 20261110-eq_final_dyn
what: Zoom 3: dynamics.

name: 20261110-eq_metric1
what: Several metrics, weighted into one.

name: 20261110-eq_metric2
what: Ours: the share of the commanded rotation followed, on three pads; 0 if dropped.

name: 20261110-eq_thesis1
what: Borras and Dollar (2015): the workspace is largest when the palm is one finger length wider than the object.

name: 20261110-eq_thesis2
what: Does the rule hold when the manipulation is executed?

name: 20261110-eq_morph1
what: A hand of the search: two distances on a 5 mm lattice, 625 hands.

name: 20261110-eq_morph2
what: Every hand on the lattice is simulated: a landscape of scores.

name: 20261110-eq_morph3
what: Each task and size has its best hand.

name: 20261110-eq_morph4
what: Does the best hand follow Borras and Dollar's rule?

name: 20261110-eq_morph5
what: The fewest hands that reach a share alpha of every task's best.

name: 20261110-eq_pads1
what: Hydroelastic contact: a pressure field from the overlap depth, summed over the patch.

name: 20261110-eq_pads2
what: Sphere pads: the same law as a sum of springs, one per 1 mm sphere.

name: 20261110-eq_outer1
what: A hand's fitness: its best controller's score, averaged over three seeds.

name: 20261110-eq_outer2
what: A generation is a population of N hands.

name: 20261110-eq_outer3
what: Keep the best half.

name: 20261110-eq_outer4
what: The best eighth are the parents.

name: 20261110-eq_outer5
what: A child is a parent moved by up to 15 mm per coordinate, on the 5 mm lattice.

name: 20261110-eq_outer6
what: The kept half and the children form the next generation.

name: 20261110-eq_inner1
what: For one hand, the inner loop searches over controllers.

name: 20261110-eq_inner2
what: The controller is HOM, held fixed: only a grasp and a few parameters remain.

name: 20261110-eq_inner3
what: Two choices: a grasp, then HOM's parameters.

name: 20261110-eq_inner4
what: The foundational pose: the grasp farthest from every constraint.

name: 20261110-eq_inner5
what: Sixteen candidate grasps per hand.

name: 20261110-eq_inner6
what: HOM: the joint speeds that best produce each fingertip's contact motion.

name: 20261110-eq_inner7
what: Press with force F through the servo's spring.

name: 20261110-eq_inner8
what: What tuning changes: the forces and the contact-mode weights.

name: 20261110-eq_inner9
what: The cross-entropy method: sample, keep the elite, refit.

name: 20261110-eq_sim1
what: A simulator stands in for the real dynamics, so that the simulated score predicts the real one.

name: 20261110-eq_sim2
what: The simulator's contact c, servo p and sensing s are calibrated on hardware.

name: 20261110-eq_sim3
what: Rollouts per EA generation: one GPU batch.

name: 20261110-eq_sim4
what: Sensing depends on the hand.
